item.title: FBI Warns of ARTEX AI Intrusion Automation as Framework Spreads Widely
item.content:encoded:
Window: 13 Nov 19:00 → 13 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

ARTEX and beyond: AI-enabled penetration testing platforms — Should Read

Cisco Talos reports that ARTEX, an AI-enabled penetration-testing framework, is being abused by criminal and China-linked actors to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, cloud abuse, and post-compromise activity at machine speed. Organizations should prioritize identity and secrets protection, monitoring for rapid anomalous activity, and preplanned containment measures.

  • Cisco Talos reports that ARTEX is an AI-enabled penetration-testing framework that can use planner and worker agents to automate reconnaissance, vulnerability testing, and follow-on actions with limited operator input.
  • Public reporting and Talos observations associate ARTEX activity with financially motivated cybercriminals and China-nexus actors, including VAPOR PANDA, Storm-0940, and Storm-3358.
  • Reported ARTEX campaigns have used password spraying, exposed or stolen credentials, and application or authorization flaws to target organizations in sectors including government, finance, telecommunications, defense, pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and technology.
  • Talos identified more than 2,500 ARTEX-associated C2 IP addresses and observed overlapping infrastructure with tools including VShell, AdaptixC2, Mimikatz, Cobalt Strike, GoPhish, and Fscan.
  • Talos recommends protecting credentials and exposed secrets, hardening public-facing systems and cloud resources, monitoring for rapid unusual activity, and preparing procedures for fast containment.

Technologies: orchestration, cloud-platform, secrets-manager, identity-provider, source-control, remote-access

Products: artex, pentagi, hephaestus, microsoft-365, azure-key-vault, amazon-cognito, amazon-s3, amazon-cloudwatch, connectwise

Vendors: cisco, microsoft, connectwise, amazon-web-services, github

City of Osaka warns of data breach impacting 1 million as Japan reels from dozens of cyber incidents — Should Read

A breach of Arara’s email distribution service exposed more than 1 million email addresses linked to Osaka’s administrative platform and potentially 77 million addresses across nearly 400 Japanese organizations. The incident is part of a wider surge in cyberattacks prompting Japan to fund stronger national cyber defenses and faster breach reporting.

  • Osaka said that hackers accessed Arara’s email distribution service, used by TKC Corporation for the city’s online administrative services platform, exposing more than 1 million email addresses.
  • The city said the leaked addresses belonged to people who received emails from its system between July 2026 and October 31, and warned residents not to open suspicious links or attachments in messages claiming to be from Osaka.
  • Arara said a November 2 cyberattack exposed 77 million email addresses from nearly 400 customers, including TKC and Sega, and was used to send millions of malicious emails impersonating credit card companies and financial institutions.
  • Japan’s prime minister announced emergency cybersecurity measures, including increased use of AI for defense, stronger information gathering, offensive cyber operations, victim support, and about $62 million in emergency funding.
  • Mihoko Matsubara of NTT said October accounted for 58% of Japan’s reported cyber incidents this year and that about 380 million pieces of personal data had been stolen so far this year.

Products: arara-email-distribution-service

Vendors: arara, tkc

Trezor confirms crypto-stealing implants in three wallets, releases fix — Should Read

Trezor confirmed that three Safe 5 wallets sold by Indonesian reseller CryptoBilis contained cellular-connected hardware implants that could steal recovery phrases and passphrases. Firmware 2.13.1 blocks the known implants, but affected buyers should move funds to a new wallet because previously captured recovery phrases remain exposed.

  • Trezor confirmed that three Safe 5 wallets sold by Indonesian reseller CryptoBilis contained malicious hardware implants designed to capture recovery phrases and passphrases.
  • The implants used an extra circuit board between the wallet’s main board and display to monitor screen activity, encrypt captured information, and send it through a mobile network to an attacker-controlled server.
  • Trezor released firmware version 2.13.1 on November 11, which it says prevents the identified implants from capturing information on updated devices.
  • The update cannot protect recovery phrases that may have been captured before installation, and Trezor advises CryptoBilis customers to move cryptocurrency to a newly created wallet with a new recovery phrase.
  • Trezor reduced its global reseller network by about 80% and is offering replacement devices to customers who purchased a Trezor wallet from CryptoBilis since March 2026.

Products: trezor-safe-5, trezor-firmware-2-13-1

Vendors: trezor, cryptobilis, ledger

Healthcare Security at Machine Speed: $17M Ransomware & AI Adversaries — Optional

A Bishop Fox-sponsored healthcare security panel discusses how organizations can prepare for AI-enabled threats, ransomware, and medical-device risks while adopting AI safely.

  • The article promotes an on-demand virtual healthcare security session provided by Bishop Fox, a Health-ISAC Community Services Champion.
  • Bishop Fox AVP Consulting Zach Moreno moderates the panel.
  • The panel includes Farzan Karimi of Moderna, Rose Lee of BlueCross BlueShield of Tennessee, and Matthew B. Welling of Holland & Knight.
  • Panelists discuss preparing healthcare security programs for AI-enabled threats while helping their organizations adopt AI safely.
  • The session also addresses ransomware and medical-device risks as factors reshaping healthcare readiness.

item.title: Check Point PHP2Shell Wiper Attacks Lead Digest Alongside Gootloader Takedown
item.content:encoded:
Window: 13 Nov 15:00 → 13 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Check Point gateways hacked via PHP2Shell to deploy VMware ESXi wiper — Must Read

Attackers exploited PHP2Shell flaws and a Check Point Security Gateway zero-day to gain root access, move to VMware ESXi hosts, and deploy the destroy_v6 data wiper against Israeli organizations. Organizations should urgently apply Check Point’s November Jumbo Hotfix and investigate exposed Mobile Access gateways for compromise indicators.

  • Attackers targeted vulnerable Check Point Security Gateway instances using the PHP2Shell flaws to gain access through Mobile Access portals and then used CVE-2026-123039 to obtain root privileges.
  • The first exploitation wave began on October 30 and initially targeted Israeli organizations, while a second wave on November 2 affected companies in multiple countries and sectors.
  • In attacks against Israeli organizations, the threat actor used the gogo scanner to locate VMware ESXi hosts and deployed the destroy_v6 wiper, which recursively deletes target data and can overwrite it with zeros first.
  • The attackers installed PHP webshells and the TSGA backdoor, which uses a component called TSProxy to receive commands hidden in ordinary network traffic.
  • Check Point recommends installing the November Jumbo Hotfix on all Management Servers and Security Gateways, especially internet-facing Mobile Access portals, and checking exposed gateways for indicators of compromise.

Technologies: firewall, remote-access, hypervisor

Products: check-point-security-gateway, mobile-access, vmware-esxi, php

Vendors: check-point, vmware, php

The Take-Home Test That Runs on Your Work Laptop: Inside the AccuraSoftHire Fake Interview Campaign — Should Read

A fake hiring operation called AccuraSoftHire used poisoned npm packages, fake coding tests, a camera "driver," and a browser extension to infect developer machines with the PolinRider loader, which retrieves rotating command servers through Ethereum transactions. Organizations should hunt for the listed packages, VS Code auto-run tasks, job-new-alerts extension, and associated IPs, then rotate all credentials and inspect repositories if an infection is found.

  • JFrog documented a fake company called AccuraSoftHire that used job ads, verified-looking recruiter profiles, coding assignments, a camera “driver,” and a browser extension to persuade candidates to run malicious code.
  • The campaign’s PolinRider loader retrieves its server address from transactions sent by an Ethereum wallet, then downloads and runs additional code from that server.
  • Two malicious npm packages used in the interview tasks, tailwind-lines-clamps and tailwind-lineclamp, remained available for about seven and five months respectively and recorded more than 4,000 downloads combined in 2026.
  • The Ethereum wallet associated with the loader posted eight server addresses between July 25 and October 19, with 103.179.142.155 identified as the newest address in the article’s analysis.
  • Binance reported that a fake job interview led an engineer to run malicious code on a work computer, and the attacker later reached its internal wallet signing service and stole about $6.34 billion from hot wallets.

Technologies: package-registry, source-control, browser, ci-cd

Products: npm, github, visual-studio-code, google-chrome, microsoft-edge, tailwind-css, homebrew, pyenv, dev-machine-guard, secure-registry, harden-runner

Vendors: github, microsoft, google, tailwind-labs, homebrew-project, jfrog, stepscurity

PostgreSQL Patches 52 Flaws, Including 22-Year-Old Bug Enabling Authenticated RCE — Should Read

PostgreSQL released security updates fixing 52 flaws, including CVE-2026-6460, a 22-year-old type-confusion bug that can allow authenticated users with object-creation privileges to execute code as the PostgreSQL operating-system user. Administrators should update supported releases immediately and rebuild C-language extensions to ensure the fix is effective.

  • PostgreSQL released updates that fix 52 security flaws, including CVE-2026-6460, a type-confusion issue with a CVSS score of 8.8.
  • CVE-2026-6460 can allow a database user able to create objects to run code with the operating-system permissions of the user running PostgreSQL.
  • PostgreSQL versions before 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected by CVE-2026-6460.
  • Administrators should update PostgreSQL and rebuild or update all installed C-language extensions, because extensions built against older releases may not be protected by the fixes.
  • The release also fixes CVE-2026-116322, which can allow an unauthenticated client to restart a PostgreSQL 18 server.

Technologies: database, cloud-platform

Products: postgresql, amazon-rds, amazon-aurora, azure-database-for-postgresql, alloydb

Vendors: postgresql-global-development-group, red-hat, aws, microsoft, google, supabase, databricks, ubicloud

ARTEX: Attackers Adopted This AI Pentesting Tool in Three Months. Leaked Secrets Are Its Fastest Way In. — Should Read

ARTEX, an AI-driven penetration-testing framework, was adopted by state-linked and criminal groups within months, with attackers most often gaining rapid access through exposed secrets, weak development credentials, and trusted application tokens. Organizations should rotate leaked credentials, replace long-lived CI keys with OIDC, eliminate production-accessible development accounts, and verify that any ARTEX deployment did not use a backdoored Docker image.

  • ARTEX is an AI-driven penetration-testing framework that coordinates agents to plan attacks, run scanning and exploitation tools, and record findings under human direction.
  • Within three months of ARTEX appearing on GitHub, reported users included Chinese state-aligned groups and criminal groups targeting hundreds of organizations, particularly financial institutions and technology firms.
  • Microsoft reported that AI agents searched public GitHub repositories for exposed credentials and, in at least one case, used a found secret to steal data from an Azure Key Vault within five minutes.
  • A WorkOS internal sales tool was accessed after a researcher's ARTEX agent found an internet-facing system that accepted a predictable development credential, then retrieved customer-related records.
  • After the original ARTEX repository was removed, a GitHub copy redirected installations to a backdoored Docker image that was pulled about 9,131 times and could run commands as root before password verification.

Technologies: container-platform, source-control, cloud-platform, secrets-manager, identity-provider, iam, ci-cd, backup

Products: artex, scopesentry, azure-key-vault, microsoft-entra-id, github-actions, docker-hub, connectwise-cloud-backup, harden-runner

Vendors: autumn-27, microsoft, github, docker, connectwise, workos, anthropic, openai, deepseek, stepsecurity

DOJ: Gootloader used in at least 44 ransomware attacks costing $29 million since 2018 — Should Read

An international Operation Endgame effort disrupted Gootloader infrastructure, which the DOJ says infected 25,000 devices and enabled at least 44 U.S. ransomware incidents causing $28.8 million in losses since 2018.

  • An international law-enforcement and cybersecurity coalition disrupted 235 servers and 257 domains linked to Gootloader, StealC, and CastleRAT.
  • The U.S. Justice Department said it removed Gootloader from more than 100 servers, including compromised websites, and seized domains used to deliver and control the malware.
  • Gootloader has operated since 2018 and infected about 25,000 devices globally, according to Justice Department officials.
  • The DOJ said Gootloader was the initial infection method in more than 44 U.S.-based ransomware cases that caused $28.8 million in losses.
  • The operation was part of Operation Endgame, an international initiative targeting malware operations and large networks of infected computers.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: gootloader, stealc, castlerat

New Mior and Skyfall Attacks Let Rogue Cloud Hosts Steal Secrets From AMD SEV-SNP VMs — Should Read

Researchers disclosed Mior and Skyfall, two flaws that let a malicious cloud host extract secrets from AMD SEV-SNP confidential VMs; Mior can additionally alter VM memory and forge attestation reports when BIOS control is available. AMD has released or scheduled firmware and microcode fixes, so cloud providers and server owners should apply vendor BIOS updates promptly.

  • Researchers disclosed Mior and Skyfall, two attacks that can allow a malicious host or hypervisor to read data from AMD SEV-SNP-protected virtual machines.
  • Mior requires control of both the hypervisor and BIOS plus a PCIe device, and researchers demonstrated that it can enable VM debugging, read or modify VM memory, and substitute a harmless VM measurement into a malicious VM’s attestation report.
  • Skyfall uses transient scheduler attacks after a hypervisor deliberately causes a VM startup failure, allowing recovery of saved register values and, in testing, a disk-encryption key.
  • AMD tracks Mior as CVE-2026-0462 and Skyfall’s VM register-data leak as CVE-2026-40671, and has issued or planned SEV firmware, microcode, and platform firmware updates for affected EPYC product lines.
  • Because the fixes are delivered through host firmware and BIOS updates, customers renting confidential VMs depend on cloud providers and server makers to deploy them.

Technologies: hypervisor, cloud-platform

Products: amd-sev-snp, amd-epyc, edk-ii, instinct-mi300a

Vendors: amd, supermicro, edk-ii-project

German military drone operations disrupted by cyberattack — Should Read

German drone maker Quantum Systems says it contained a cyberattack involving a malicious update to its QBase ground-control software, prompting precautionary grounding of some military drones. The company believes its support for Ukraine made it a target, though no attacker has been identified.

  • Quantum Systems detected an active cyberattack by hostile actors in late October and said it worked with authorities to restore its unmanned systems safely.
  • Reports citing internal sources said the compromise involved a malicious update file for QBase, Quantum Systems’ ground-control and mission-planning software, distributed through the company’s update server.
  • Germany’s armed forces reportedly grounded Quantum Systems drones as a precaution and excluded the company’s systems from a recent military exercise.
  • Quantum Systems said it believes its announced support for Ukraine contributed to it being targeted, but it did not attribute the incident to a specific actor.
  • German military counterintelligence, domestic intelligence, and the federal cybersecurity agency are reportedly involved in the response.

Products: qbase, vector, falke

Vendors: quantum-systems, cubepilot

German parliament passes law giving spy agencies hacking, sabotage powers — Should Read

Germany’s Bundestag passed a major intelligence-law overhaul giving the BND and BfV expanded authority for hacking, sabotage, data analysis, and biometric matching, subject to oversight and limits on harming people. The law is framed as a response to foreign espionage, cyber operations, and disinformation threats, particularly linked to Russia.

  • Germany’s Bundestag passed legislation by 308 votes to 190, with 71 abstentions, expanding the powers of the BND and BfV.
  • The law permits the BND to conduct actions abroad such as hacking foreign systems, disrupting adversaries’ supply chains, and taking down servers used by hostile state-backed hackers.
  • The BfV can block or reroute data traffic within Germany but remains prohibited from using force against people.
  • Both agencies can analyze large datasets with AI and conduct biometric image matching against material found online.
  • Hacking operations and active measures inside Germany require advance approval from the Independent Control Council, whose court-like panel was expanded from six to twelve members.

TSMC confirms employee data breach tied to cloud service provider — Should Read

TSMC confirmed that a breach at an unnamed cloud service provider exposed data on current and former employees, including reportedly contact, identification, and banking details. The company said its own systems, operations, and customer data were not compromised.

  • TSMC confirmed that a breach at an unnamed cloud service provider exposed information matching data held in that provider’s system services for current and former employees.
  • TSMC stated that its own systems were not compromised and that the exposed information was unrelated to company operations or customer data.
  • A hacker forum post on November 8 offered 6.9 GB of alleged TSMC employee data, reportedly including contact, identification, and banking information, for 3 BTC.
  • TSMC said it is notifying affected personnel and working with the cloud vendor, investigating authorities, and a third-party cybersecurity agency.
  • TSMC previously faced a 2023 ransomware incident involving an IT hardware supplier and fired two employees last year over suspected theft of trade secrets.

Technologies: cloud-platform

University of Texas at Arlington warns personal information stolen during cyberattack — Should Read

The University of Texas at Arlington confirmed that hackers stole personal information in a recent cyberattack, with the Qilin ransomware gang claiming responsibility. The university is assessing whose data was affected while its MachForms portal remains offline.

  • The University of Texas at Arlington confirmed that personal information was stolen during a cybersecurity incident last month.
  • The university is determining whose information was involved and what data was accessed, and says it will notify affected individuals directly.
  • UTA took its MachForms portal offline after announcing the incident, and the portal remains unavailable.
  • The Qilin ransomware gang claimed responsibility for the attack on UTA.
  • Other universities, including York University and Vanderbilt University, are also investigating recent incidents involving data theft or operational disruption.

Products: machforms

NYC to bar surveillance pricing as momentum for bans grows nationwide — May Read

New York City approved a ban on surveillance pricing, restricting businesses from using consumers’ personal data to charge different prices for the same goods or services. The move follows Seattle’s ban and adds momentum to similar state and federal scrutiny of algorithmic, data-driven pricing practices.

  • The New York City Council voted 44–5 to approve a bill barring businesses from using consumers’ personal data to charge different prices for the same product.
  • The bill permits fines of up to $1,000 per violation and exempts legitimate, transparent discounts such as loyalty-program, student, veteran, and buy-one-get-one-free offers.
  • Seattle passed a similar surveillance-pricing ban the previous month, while New Jersey, Connecticut, and Maryland already have related laws.
  • The Federal Trade Commission ordered nine food delivery, airline, ride-sharing, and retail companies, including Uber, DoorDash, Walmart, Target, and major airlines, to provide information about their use of personal data in pricing.
  • Consumer Reports reported that Kroger collects data on loyalty-program members to create shopper profiles and sells data to third parties for targeted advertising; Kroger denies using personal data to change prices.

Vendors: kroger, uber, doordash, walmart, target

How one AI agent exposed five critical enterprise security gaps — Optional

Sponsored guidance from Token Security argues that unmanaged AI agents can create major enterprise risks when they use persistent credentials, process untrusted inputs, and can modify sensitive systems. Organizations should inventory agents, enforce least-privilege identities and approval controls, monitor behavior rather than permissions alone, and retain audit trails.

  • A Cloud Security Alliance survey commissioned by Token Security found that 82% of 418 IT and security professionals had discovered AI agents in their environments that they did not know about during the prior year.
  • The article describes a hypothetical accounts-payable AI agent that reads an inbox, matches invoices in an ERP system, and posts daily summaries to Slack using OAuth grants, a personal API key, and a Slack connector.
  • The article says the agent violates the Agents Rule of Two because it processes untrusted email, accesses private vendor bank information, and can modify ERP records without human review.
  • A malicious invoice containing hidden text could instruct the agent to change a vendor's bank details, while logs would show authorized tools and valid credentials.
  • The article recommends detecting suspicious agent behavior by comparing actions to the agent's established behavior, such as its first use of an ERP write function or a new sequence of reading email followed by changing a payment record.

Technologies: iam, pam

Vendors: token-security, datarobot, meta

Top 8 Upwind Security alternatives for code and cloud security — Optional

The article positions Aikido Security as the leading Upwind alternative for organizations seeking integrated cloud and code security, emphasizing AutoFix, IDE checks, authenticated DAST and AI pentesting. It compares Wiz, Sysdig, Orca, Cortex Cloud, Sweet, Aqua and Microsoft Defender for Cloud by their cloud, runtime, remediation and developer-security strengths.

  • Upwind is presented as a runtime-first cloud security platform built around an eBPF sensor, with code-security capabilities such as SAST and DAST added in late 2026.
  • The article says Aikido Security combines code and cloud findings in one workspace and offers AutoFix pull requests for supported code, dependency, infrastructure-as-code, and container findings.
  • Aikido is described as providing authenticated and unauthenticated DAST plus AI pentesting intended to identify logic-level problems such as broken access control and multi-step attack chains.
  • Wiz and Orca are described as cloud-first platforms that connect cloud risks to source code and offer fix pull requests for supported findings.
  • Sysdig Secure, Cortex Cloud, Sweet Security, Aqua Security, and Microsoft Defender for Cloud are highlighted for differing runtime investigation, response, enforcement, or Microsoft-environment capabilities.

item.title: SilentAir Telecom Interception, ActiveCloud Ransomware, and UK Cyber Incident Records
item.content:encoded:
Window: 13 Nov 11:00 → 13 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users — Should Read

Enea uncovered SilentAir, a suspected state-backed espionage group that compromised equipment at Asian telecom operators to redirect calls and SMS, intercept 2FA codes, and conduct large-scale silent-SMS surveillance, with Taiwan as its main target. The activity may be linked to China and overlaps with infrastructure previously associated with Liminal Panda, though attribution remains unconfirmed.

  • Enea identified SilentAir, a suspected state-level group that used compromised equipment at mobile operators in at least six Asian countries to intercept selected calls and text messages, primarily targeting people in Taiwan.
  • SilentAir redirected victims' communications by sending network messages that falsely claimed compromised equipment was serving a target's phone, and Enea observed two-factor authentication codes being intercepted after some diversions succeeded.
  • SilentAir sent silent text messages at large scale, mainly to Taiwanese subscribers, apparently including tests to confirm whether text-message diversions were working.
  • Enea assesses only with low confidence that SilentAir is linked to China, citing its focus on Taiwan, avoidance of Chinese networks, and activity patterns aligned with a UTC+8 working schedule and Chinese holidays.
  • The activity overlapped at some operators with known Liminal Panda infections, but Enea said a connection between SilentAir and Liminal Panda remains possible rather than confirmed.

Technologies: firewall, network-monitoring

Products: gtpdoor, sctpe, sigweaver

Vendors: enea, crowdstrike

Ransomware attack on Belarusian cloud firm disrupts businesses for days — Should Read

Belarusian cloud provider ActiveCloud suffered a ransomware attack that disrupted websites, email, and virtual servers for businesses nationwide, though it says core services have been restored and found no evidence of customer data theft. The incident follows similar recent attacks on Russian hosting providers ESTT and Beget, with no confirmed link among them.

  • Belarusian cloud provider ActiveCloud said a ransomware attack encrypted parts of its infrastructure and disrupted customer websites, corporate email, virtual servers, and support channels.
  • ActiveCloud disclosed the incident on Tuesday and said on Friday that its main services had been restored, although some customers could still face problems recovering their virtual machines.
  • ActiveCloud said its investigation found no evidence that customer data was stolen and did not identify the attackers or explain how they accessed its systems.
  • Smartpress and Domino’s Pizza in Belarus were among organizations affected by service disruptions linked to ActiveCloud’s outage.
  • The incident followed recent attacks on Russian hosting providers ESTT and Beget, but no public evidence has linked the three incidents.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: e-cloud, e-cloud-protected, smartmail

Vendors: activecloud, estt, beget

Record number of cyber incidents reported to UK privacy regulator — Optional

UK organizations reported a record 1,371 cyber incidents to the Information Commissioner’s Office in the third quarter, signaling a likely new annual high. Security researchers attribute the increase in part to rising data-theft extortion activity, with UK victims increasingly listed on criminal leak sites.

  • The UK Information Commissioner’s Office recorded 1,371 cyber incidents from July through September, the highest total for any three-month period in its published data.
  • Reports of all data-security incidents, including non-cyber mistakes such as emails sent to the wrong recipient, reached a quarterly record of 4,604.
  • Sophos said about 350 UK organizations had been named on criminal leak sites so far that year, roughly 50% more than in the prior year.
  • Retail and manufacturing incidents rose from 205 in the second quarter to 296 in the third quarter, while reports involving charities and voluntary organizations increased from 79 to 145.
  • The ICO opened formal investigations into 18 of the 1,371 cyber incidents reported in the third quarter, while most cases were closed with informal action.

Technologies: mfa

Vendors: sophos

When an AI Agent Goes Wrong, Can You Stop It? — Optional

Stopping an AI agent requires more than disabling the model: teams must halt workflows and queued jobs, revoke credentials and sessions, disable risky tools, restrict network access, and preserve evidence. Organizations should test these containment controls in advance and restore access only after identifying and fixing the underlying issue.

  • An AI agent may have access to records and connected tools that allow it to act on instructions embedded in a support ticket, including exporting data to an unfamiliar destination.
  • Disabling an AI model may not stop queued jobs, retries, established sessions, credentials, or separate services that have already received work.
  • Effective containment may require stopping active and queued runs, revoking associated credentials and sessions, disabling relevant tools or integrations, and restricting network connections.
  • Teams should preserve agent, identity, API, application, and network records to distinguish attempted actions from completed actions and determine what was accessed or changed.
  • Before restoring an agent workflow, organizations should identify the cause, restore only the minimum access needed, test in a controlled environment, and monitor activity after resumption.

Technologies: pam, secrets-manager

Products: keeperpam, keeper-secrets-manager

Vendors: keeper-security, owasp

Top 9 Qualys alternatives for infrastructure and application security — Optional

Teams replacing or supplementing Qualys often seek simpler pricing, cloud-native coverage, developer-friendly remediation, and better prioritization than traditional asset-based vulnerability management provides. The best alternative depends on whether the need is code-to-cloud security, infrastructure scanning, cloud attack-path analysis, or authenticated web and API testing.

  • Qualys is primarily built for network and host vulnerability management and compliance, while cloud-native coverage is provided through its separate TotalCloud module.
  • Teams seek Qualys alternatives because its per-asset, module-by-module pricing can be difficult to forecast, and its workflows can leave developers with long lists of findings and no proposed code fixes.
  • Aikido Security combines code, cloud, container, and application testing capabilities and can open pull requests with proposed fixes for supported code, dependency, infrastructure-as-code, and container findings.
  • Tenable and Rapid7 InsightVM focus on infrastructure vulnerabilities, while Wiz and Orca Security focus on cloud risk and Snyk focuses on developer-facing code and dependency security.
  • Invicti specializes in authenticated web application and API testing, whereas Greenbone OpenVAS Community Edition provides self-managed open-source network and host assessment.

Technologies: cloud-platform, ci-cd, source-control

item.title: ESXi Destruction Campaigns and Critical Apache HTTP/2 RCE Lead Security Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 13 Nov 07:00 → 13 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell Flaws in Check Point Gateways to Deploy TSGA Backdoor and Wipe ESXi Files — Must Read

Attackers exploited unpatched PHP2Shell flaws and a Gaia OS privilege-escalation vulnerability on Check Point gateways to deploy the TSGA backdoor, then in some cases pivoted to VMware ESXi hosts to run destructive wiper malware. The campaign initially targeted Israeli organizations before expanding globally, with possible but unconfirmed links to China-aligned actors.

  • An unknown threat actor exploited PHP2Shell vulnerabilities in unpatched Check Point Security Gateways and used CVE-2026-123039 in Gaia OS to gain root-level control.
  • The campaign began on October 30, 2026, against Israeli organizations and expanded on November 2 to organizations in multiple countries and sectors.
  • Attackers deployed PHP web shells and the TSGA backdoor, which includes TSProxy and supports encrypted remote access, configuration theft, persistence, process injection, and firewall-log tampering.
  • In some compromises, the attackers used SSH access to move from a Check Point gateway to a VMware ESXi host, where they executed the destroy_v6 wiper and dropped DREAM_ANNEXATION.txt notes.
  • Check Point said the TSGA and TSProxy components resemble the PhiliKit toolkit associated with the China-nexus group Armory Castle, but it could not confidently attribute the campaign.

Technologies: firewall, vpn, remote-access, operating-system, hypervisor

Products: check-point-security-gateways, gaia-os, check-point-mobile-access, vmware-esxi

Vendors: check-point, vmware

Critical Apache HTTP Server vulnerability can allow remote code execution (CVE-2026-119618) — Must Read

Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.55–2.4.70 with HTTP/2 enabled are affected by critical unauthenticated remote code execution flaw CVE-2026-119618; upgrade to 2.4.71 or later immediately, or disable HTTP/2 until patching is possible.

  • CVE-2026-119618 is a critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server's HTTP/2 module that can allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code.
  • Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 are affected, and version 2.4.71 and later contain the fix.
  • The flaw is a race condition in the assign_headers() function that can cause heap corruption and be turned into remote code execution.
  • Organizations that cannot patch immediately can reduce exposure by disabling HTTP/2 and restricting Apache to HTTP/1.1.
  • The article states that there were no reports of exploitation in the wild at the time of publication.

Technologies: web-server

Products: apache-http-server, mod-http2

Vendors: apache-software-foundation, github

Ransomware at the hypervisor layer: how attackers use ESXi and vCenter features for malicious purposes — Should Read

A BlackNevas ransomware operation destroyed a virtualized environment by compromising vCenter and abusing legitimate VMware management features to enable ESXi SSH access, disrupt backups, and wipe virtual-machine data without exploiting a hypervisor vulnerability. The key defense is to treat vCenter, ESXi administration, and backup recovery as separate high-trust security boundaries with isolated identities, restricted access, and remotely retained telemetry.

  • The attackers used legitimate VMware management interfaces rather than exploiting a hypervisor vulnerability, enabling ESXi SSH through vCenter Host Profiles before directly accessing target hosts.
  • After accessing a vCenter appliance through SSH as root, the attackers deployed MeshAgent and later installed a Ligolo-ng reverse tunnel as a persistent systemd service disguised as vmware-vdma.
  • The ransomware payload was delivered to ESXi through SFTP, staged under /tmp, tested roughly three hours before detonation, and then executed against the /vmfs virtual-machine storage path.
  • The attackers disrupted backup infrastructure before the ESXi impact by disabling antivirus protection, stopping backup services, encrypting recovery systems, and disrupting administrative access.

Attackers exploited unpatched Check Point Mobile Access gateways using PHP2Shell and CVE-2026-123039, deploying PhiliKit-linked TSGA/TSProxy backdoors and, in some Israeli intrusions, pivoting to ESXi hosts to run the destroy_v6 wiper.   • After initial access, the attackers exploited CVE-2026-123039 in the DynamicCLI interface to gain root-level control and installed PHP webshells plus the TSGA and TSProxy backdoors.
  • The attackers used the gogo scanner to identify internal systems, accessed a VMware ESXi host over SSH using the vpxuser account, and executed the destroy_v6 wiper in the destructive stage.
  • The first wave focused on Israeli organizations and included destructive activity in some cases, while a November 2 wave targeted organizations in multiple countries without observed destructive activity.
  • TSGA and TSProxy share code, configuration, and cryptographic material with the PhiliKit framework, but the article states that the operation’s true nature and attribution cannot be assessed with high confidence.

CVE-2026-126187: React Server Components Flaw Lets Attackers Execute Code Through Smuggled Flight Rows — Must Read

React Server Components packages before 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9, and 19.3.1 reportedly contain a critical Flight transport framing flaw that can enable unauthenticated server-side code execution under specific shared-ArrayBuffer conditions. Upgrade affected React/framework dependencies, rebuild and redeploy, and avoid sending multiple typed-array views over a shared ArrayBuffer until patched.

  • CVE-2026-126187 is described as a critical, unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in React Server Components, with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.5.
  • The affected packages are react-server-dom-webpack, react-server-dom-parcel, and react-server-dom-turbopack in versions through 19.0.8, 19.1.9, 19.2.8, and 19.3.0.
  • The issue requires a response containing multiple typed-array views over a shared ArrayBuffer, attacker-influenced bytes in one view, and a downstream path that transfers the backing storage.
  • React fixed the issue in versions 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9, and 19.3.1 by copying large typed-array payloads into exact-size buffers before sending them.
  • Organizations should upgrade framework-managed or direct dependencies, confirm the resolved package versions in lockfiles, and rebuild and redeploy affected applications.

Mass bomb-hoax emails targeting schools, airports and newsrooms across Europe were sent through compromised accounts at legitimate institutions, helping them bypass email checks and complicating attribution. Authorities deem the threats non-credible, but cross-border investigations are challenged by anonymized access and slow international evidence requests.

  • Authorities in Scotland and Ireland assessed the school threats as not credible, while the messages nonetheless prompted evacuations in Italy.

WFX Phantom: The GitHub Actions Secret Stealer That Deletes Its Tracks — Must Read

WFX Phantom is a large-scale GitHub Actions secret-stealing campaign that uses stolen developer and bot tokens to inject a CI payload, steal secrets and cloud credentials, then quickly revert commits and delete workflow runs. Organizations should immediately hunt for its PR and commit indicators, treat affected workflow-accessible credentials as compromised, and remove AWS/Azure persistence mechanisms.

  • Beginning November 10, 2026, attackers used stolen GitHub tokens to add the WFX secret stealer to repositories where those tokens had write access, then typically reverted the commit and deleted the associated GitHub Actions run within a minute.
  • The campaign used probe pull requests titled "docs: dependency audit notes" from branches named "wfx-docs"; GitHub search showed more than 63,000 such pull requests as of November 12, although only some repositories received the payload.
  • WFX collects GitHub Actions secrets, runner-process memory, cloud credentials, repository data, and recent workflow artifacts, and it can attempt persistence through AWS role-policy changes, IAM access keys, and Azure federated identity credentials.
  • The payload was hidden in modified workflows, existing shell scripts, new audit workflow files, or hidden .ci-*.sh scripts executed through npm hooks, allowing it to run even when a workflow file was not visibly changed.
  • Later samples sent stolen data exclusively to a Telegram chat through api.telegram.org, so blocking the campaign's previously observed collection IP addresses alone no longer stopped the newest versions.

Technologies: ci-cd, source-control, iam, cloud-platform, secrets-manager, package-registry

Critical Pre-Auth MongoDB Flaw (CVE-2026-118383) Can Crash Lagging Servers on Failover — Must Read

MongoDB has patched CVE-2026-118383, a critical pre-authentication use-after-free flaw that can crash a replica-set member if it later becomes primary while behind on replication. Organizations should upgrade all self-managed replica-set members promptly and restrict database network access until patched.

  • MongoDB has released fixed versions for CVE-2026-118383, a critical use-after-free flaw rated 9.5 out of 10 that can be triggered by two unauthenticated requests.
  • The flaw affects MongoDB replica-set members, including shard and configuration server members in sharded clusters, but does not affect standalone mongod servers.
  • A targeted member crashes only if it later wins an election to become primary while it is behind on recent changes, causing cleanup during catch-up to reuse memory that has already been freed.
  • Datadog Security Labs reproduced the issue in a lab and found that enabling authentication on vulnerable versions did not block the two requests.
  • MongoDB Atlas clusters receive fixed versions automatically during maintenance, while self-managed deployments must upgrade every replica-set member and should restrict database network access until they can patch.

Technologies: database, cloud-platform

Products: mongodb-server, mongodb-atlas

Vendors: mongodb, datadog

Node.js Fixes 16 Flaws, Including HTTP/2 Bugs That Crash Servers and Leak Other Connections' Data — Must Read

Node.js released security updates for supported 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x lines that fix 16 flaws, including critical HTTP/2 and HTTPS issues that can crash servers, leak cross-connection memory, and potentially expose TLS private keys. Organizations running Node.js servers should upgrade to 22.23.5, 24.22.3, or 26.13.1 immediately, as no workarounds are listed and end-of-life versions remain unpatched.

  • Node.js released versions 22.23.5, 24.22.3, and 26.13.1 to fix 16 vulnerabilities, seven of which are rated high severity.
  • CVE-2026-123863 can let an unauthenticated client crash default Node.js HTTP/2 servers on the 24.x and 26.x lines when the server responds before a request body has fully arrived.
  • CVE-2026-123866 can cause affected Node.js HTTP/2 servers to send a client memory contents that may include responses intended for other connections.
  • CVE-2026-123864 affects Node.js HTTPS servers and may allow an unauthenticated client to read memory from other connections, including TLS private keys and other users’ requests, under specified handler conditions.
  • Node.js lists updating as the only fix, provides no workaround for servers that cannot update, and says end-of-life lines including 20.x and 25.x remain affected.

Products: node-js

Vendors: node-js, anthropic

Attackers turn NIKKE’s game launcher into malware — Should Read

Attackers abused NIKKE’s legitimate server-pushed launcher task channel to deliver a Lua-based infostealer disguised as a log file, allowing credential, crypto-wallet, and developer-secret theft from within the signed launcher process. Players who used the launcher during the attack window should treat their systems as compromised and rotate affected credentials and wallet seeds.

  • Attackers abused NIKKE’s legitimate server-pushed task channel to make its launcher download a malicious LuaJIT payload disguised as a normal log file.
  • The payload, called k2f-agent by Bitdefender, ran inside the signed launcher process and included 46 modules for credential theft, file collection, remote commands, and cleanup.
  • The stealer targeted saved passwords and cookies from Chrome, Edge, and Opera, five cryptocurrency wallet browser extensions, and potentially developer and system secrets such as SSH keys, GPG keys, Git credentials, and Kubernetes configurations.
  • Stolen information was sent through the launcher’s existing encrypted telemetry channel, while download, data collection, exfiltration, and cleanup occurred in less than ten minutes.
  • Bitdefender stated that its Advanced Threat Defense stopped the launcher on observed protected systems before personal information could be exfiltrated, and the Iceland-hosted malicious delivery server was later taken down.

Threat actors are increasingly abusing the legitimate GSocket remote-access tool to persist on compromised Linux web and hosting servers through outbound, encrypted relay connections that evade inbound firewall controls. Administrators should remove GSocket artifacts, audit persistence mechanisms, restrict outbound traffic, and patch exposed systems.

  • Multiple threat actors are abusing the open-source GSocket remote-access tool to retain access to Linux servers after the initial entry vulnerabilities have been patched.
  • Microsoft Defender for Endpoint telemetry recorded a 356.2% increase in GSocket-related detections between March and August.
  • GSocket routes encrypted sessions through the Global Socket Relay Network using outbound connections from both the compromised host and the attacker, so the host does not need an inbound listener or public IP address.
  • Of detected GSocket incidents, 87.1% involved web applications and hosting environments, with PHP web applications and cPanel hosting accounting for 63.9% and Apache accounting for 24.3%.
  • Microsoft recommends removing GSocket-related files, confirming relay-network connections have stopped, restricting outbound traffic, and auditing cron jobs, systemd services, and shell startup files for unauthorized additions.

Microsoft says a limited number of Windows 11 devices that installed the October 2026 preview update may fail to install November’s KB5132061 security update, showing errors including 0x800f0989 and 0x800f0993. The company says an automatic repair should resolve the issue within 24–48 hours without user action.

  • Microsoft confirmed that some Windows 11 devices are unable to complete installation of the November 2026 security update KB5132061.
  • The issue affects a limited number of devices that installed the October 2026 non-security preview update KB5127936; devices that did not install that preview update are not affected.
  • Affected devices may repeatedly attempt the update or display error codes 0x80070306, 0x800f0989, or 0x800f0993.
  • Microsoft said it would automatically repair affected devices within 24 to 48 hours beginning November 11, 2026, after which the November security update should download and install through Windows Update.

Transcending the trust boundaries: how a cloud pentest works — Optional

Effective cloud pentesting focuses on proving whether attackers can cross trust boundaries between tenant workloads, provider-managed services, control planes, and underlying infrastructure—not merely finding code execution or open ports. Tests should safely verify real cross-tenant or provider-level impact through minimal, authorized actions.

  • Cloud penetration testing should assess whether attackers can cross trust boundaries between tenant resources, provider-managed services, internal provider components, and underlying infrastructure rather than merely identify open ports or achieve code execution.
  • The article models cloud platforms in three layers: the public External layer, the provider’s logical Overlay layer for service runtimes and internal components, and the physical and virtualization-focused Underlay layer.
  • A confirmed trust-boundary violation requires more than seeing or authenticating to an internal service; the tester must obtain authorization and safely perform a controlled action outside the original boundary.
  • Service account credentials, network access, and runtime context must be evaluated together because an over-privileged credential can enable access to internal APIs even when network segmentation is strict.
  • Cloud pentests of provider infrastructure require separate authorization and should confirm cross-tenant effects only with controlled test tenants and synthetic data.

Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely — Must Read

Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55–2.4.70 has a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw in mod_http2 (CVE-2026-119618) when HTTP/2 is enabled; upgrade to 2.4.71 or disable h2/h2c until patched.

  • CVE-2026-119618 is a critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2 module that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution on servers with HTTP/2 enabled.
  • The flaw affects Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 and is fixed in version 2.4.71.
  • Red Hat released fixes for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 and 10, while Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 and earlier are not affected.
  • Debian unstable has been fixed with apache2 2.4.71-1, while Debian bookworm, trixie, and forky were listed as vulnerable and Amazon Linux releases were awaiting fixes.
  • Organizations unable to update can remove h2 and h2c from Apache's Protocols directive and leave Protocols http/1.1 as a temporary mitigation.

ScreenConnect Attacks Target at Least 288 Endpoints Across 48 Organizations With Rogue Clients — Must Read

Attackers are abusing compromised ConnectWise ScreenConnect panels or operator sessions to deploy rogue clients and the SCKit toolkit, affecting at least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations. ConnectWise disabled five third-party extensions as a precaution, while investigators have found no evidence of a ScreenConnect vulnerability or compromise of ConnectWise infrastructure.

  • ConnectWise disabled five third-party ScreenConnect extensions as a precaution after reports of unauthorized access, while stating it found no evidence of a ScreenConnect vulnerability or compromise of its own infrastructure.
  • Huntress observed attackers use cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels to deploy rogue ScreenConnect clients to at least 288 managed endpoints across 48 organizations.
  • The observed activity uses the SCKit toolkit to establish persistent remote access, create a relay mechanism for intercepting session cookies, add Microsoft Defender exclusions, and create a scheduled task named TrapWatch.
  • Huntress said available telemetry points to compromised credentials or hijacked operator sessions as possible initial access methods, although the exact method remains unclear.
  • Sophos observed unauthorized ScreenConnect client deployments from three ScreenConnect instance IDs, including commands that downloaded and silently installed a ScreenConnect client from an identified IP address.

Products: screenconnect, microsoft-defender

Can Agentic AI Investigate a Phishing Campaign? Evidence Walkthrough — Optional

Agentic AI can accelerate phishing investigations by gathering evidence across domains, cloned pages, search results, and infrastructure, but humans must validate attribution and approve any external or production actions. Because attackers can embed prompt-injection instructions in phishing content, agents need evidence trails, strict permissions, and controls that treat fetched content as untrusted data.

  • Agentic AI can independently collect phishing-investigation evidence such as domain registration details, safely captured web pages, related infrastructure, and indicators, but the article recommends human approval for actions such as blocks and takedown requests.
  • A Microsoft randomized trial involving 167 security analysts found that analysts using the Security Copilot Phishing Triage Agent found up to 6.5 times more true positives per minute and were up to 77% more accurate, although the article notes the trial used Microsoft's own product and test corpus.
  • The article uses lookalike Microsoft Teams domains, including teams-online[.]com, teams-livemeeting[.]com, and teams-cloud[.]live, to show how an investigation can connect cloned pages, young privacy-protected registrations, search placement, and a fake update lure.
  • The article warns that attackers can place hidden instructions in phishing emails, attachments, and web content intended to influence AI systems that read or summarize them.
  • It recommends treating all fetched content as untrusted data, separating read access from action permissions, requiring evidence for each verdict claim, logging tool calls, and retaining human approval for actions outside the organization.
